subject: Uptime reconciliation request & maintenance exception — AlphaHealth production impact
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir.rao@alphahealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: uptime-team@alphahealth.com
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Production latency spike / uptime reconciliation request

Hi Monica,

We saw sustained 5-10x token latency increases and a noticeable drop in successful responses for our patient-matching workflow yesterday morning (2026-12-17). Our SREs measured a degraded window from ~2026-12-17T07:22:00Z to ~2026-12-17T08:09:00Z (UTC). That aligns roughly with what our application telemetry shows: elevated p95 and error-rate spikes.

AlphaHealth is preparing a formal SLA credit request and needs Redwood's official uptime tally for the period, as well as any notes about maintenance windows, partial degradation handling, and third-party peering issues that might affect attribution. We were told by our CDN/peering vendor (ThirdPartyNet) that they performed an emergency maintenance, but we don't yet have a report.

Can you confirm:
- Redwood's measured outage/degraded window for our account (timestamps + how partial degradation is counted)
- Whether any maintenance (planned or emergency) was recorded on Redwood's side that could explain the delta
- Next steps and what data you need from us to complete reconciliation

I'm attaching a short CSV with the request window and our app-side samples (attachment: alphahealth_request_log_snippets.csv).

Thanks,
Samir Rao
Director, Platform Reliability — AlphaHealth
Samir.Rao@alphahealth.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir.rao@alphahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 10:05:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Production latency spike / uptime reconciliation request

Hi Samir — thanks for the heads up and for the log snippets. We're sorry AlphaHealth hit that degradation window.

We can do a reconciliation but need a couple of precise pieces to reduce mismatch risk:
- Confirm the exact timezone for your SRE timestamps (you listed UTC, which matches our expectation).
- If possible, send any request IDs or request hashes that show the error responses — that helps match on our side.
- Any BGP/peering incident ticket IDs from ThirdPartyNet would be helpful if you have them.

On our side we'll:
- Pull per-route token latency and error-rate tallies for your account for the 2026-12-17 06:00–10:00 UTC window.
- Check our maintenance schedule and any emergency operational notes.
- Share an initial reconciliation by EOD Monday (2026-12-20) unless we need more details.

I CC'd Ben (account lead) to keep him in the loop.

Attachments referenced: none in this message.

—
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

From: Samir Rao <samir.rao@alphahealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: uptime-team@alphahealth.com; contract-ops@alphahealth.com
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Production latency spike / uptime reconciliation request

Thanks Monica. Quick follow-up with more detail attached.

Key notes from our side:
- Our SREs confirm timestamps are UTC.
- Observed application-level degradation: 2026-12-17T07:22:14Z -> 2026-12-17T08:09:32Z (47m 18s).
- Error classes: 504 gateway and 502 for upstream timeouts; these line up with long tail token-generation times rather than model errors.
- We don't have a ThirdPartyNet ticket number yet; their ops contact (Ingrid) told us they were investigating a peering flap on the morning of 12/17.

I've attached the CSV snippet we mentioned (alphahealth_request_log_snippets.csv) — it includes sample request IDs, timestamps, and status codes.

Appreciate the help — Samir

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 10:00:00 -0800
Subject: INTERNAL: AlphaHealth reconciliation — proposed approach

Team — internal note (do not forward to customer yet).

Summary: AlphaHealth reports a 47m degraded window on 2026-12-17 (UTC). They believe a ThirdPartyNet peering flap may be involved. Action items:
1) Ben: pull per-account token latency histogram and success rate for AlphaHealth for 06:00–10:00 UTC on 12/17. Export per-API-route breakdown and list top 20 request IDs by latency.
2) Marissa: validate whether we had any scheduled maintenance on infra or routing during that window. Check dedicated pool maintenance logs and any control-plane events.
3) Evelyn: confirm how our SLA counts "partial degradation" (we currently use a 5% weighted partial threshold: see SLA appendix). If we have automatic prefix/KV cache misses during that window, quantify token cost impact.

I attached a quick spreadsheet with a suggested apportionment model (redwood_sla_calculation_v1.xlsx) — it includes three scenarios: direct-redwood, third-party-attribution, and shared-apportionment. We'll share a clear reconciliation email to AlphaHealth once we have the numbers.

Timing: aim to have a draft reconciliation to the customer by EOD Monday 12/20. If ThirdPartyNet confirms an incident, point 2b will be: request their incident report and timeline to decide exclusion under the SLA's third-party exception clause.

—Monica

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Rao <samir.rao@alphahealth.com>, uptime-team@alphahealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 19 Dec 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: AlphaHealth — initial reconciliation and next steps

Hi Samir / uptime team,

Thanks for the CSV — that was helpful. We've pulled our per-route metrics and token-level tallies for the window. Preliminary notes:
- Redwood observed elevated token p95 across your primary model route between 2026-12-17T07:24:10Z and 2026-12-17T07:54:05Z (UTC) — ~29m 55s.
- We also saw intermittent API gateway 502/504s that correlate with the high-latency tail, not with model host failures.
- Checking our maintenance logs, there were no scheduled Redwood maintenance jobs for your dedicated pool that evening.

Given the mismatch between our measured ~30m and your observed ~47m, likely factors are:
- Different aggregation method: we count continuous degraded minutes per-route with a 3-minute hysteresis; your app-level sampling captured longer tail effects.
- A subset of the time looks attributable to a peering/egress issue — we are contacting the peering provider for confirmation.

Requested from you to finalize:
- Any additional request IDs that showed backend 5xxs after 07:54:05Z UTC.
- Permission to contact ThirdPartyNet directly and share our logs (we will only share timestamps and anonymized request IDs).

I've attached an initial cut of our reconciliation CSV (alphahealth_request_log_snippets.csv) and the calculation worksheet for visibility (redwood_sla_calculation_v1.xlsx). If ThirdPartyNet confirms the peering flap and provides an incident report, we will evaluate the SLA third-party exclusion clause and propose a proportional credit if applicable.

Next step: We'll follow up as soon as ThirdPartyNet responds; if we don't have confirmation by EOD Monday 12/20, we'll propose a conservative apportionment based on overlap metrics.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ingrid P. <ingrid@thirdpartynet.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Samir Rao <samir.rao@alphahealth.com>
Cc: uptime-team@alphahealth.com, contract-ops@alphahealth.com
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: ThirdPartyNet incident report: 12/17 peering flap — initial findings

Hi Monica / Samir,

Apologies for the delay. ThirdPartyNet confirms an unplanned peering flap affecting a subset of our edge POPs on 2026-12-17 between 07:23:40Z and 07:41:20Z (UTC). Our internal BGP session reset affected a number of upstream paths and caused transient packet drops for ~17m 40s in the impacted region.

Notes:
- Root cause: an automated BGP session refresh misapplied on a routing cluster during routine config drift remediation.
- Scope: localized to three edge POPs that serve traffic to your US-east egress cluster; not a global outage.
- We are attaching an initial incident report (thirdparty_incident_report.pdf).

We see that AlphaHealth's app reported a longer window (47m); that can happen when application retries and long-tail tokenization amplify perceived duration. If you'd like, we're happy to provide BGP community logs and per-prefix reannouncement timestamps to help reconcile; please indicate a contact and a secure transfer mechanism.

We'll patch the automation to prevent recurrence and can sign an operational statement that confirms this as an upstream peering event. If Redwood's reconciliation attributes the impacted minutes to ThirdPartyNet, we will accept responsibility for the portion attributable to the peering flap.

Regards,
Ingrid P.
Incident Manager — ThirdPartyNet
ingrid@thirdpartynet.com
